summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming as its very first tool call, asked seven rounds of clarifying/decision questions, produced a decomposed design direction, and stopped to ask for approval before writing any spec or code. No implementation files were written.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are satisfied and verified against the session log rather than recollection: the brainstorming skill was the first tool call, no Write/Edit ever occurred, the working tree is unchanged, and the run ended with the agent asking for approval to write a spec — one of the story's defined completion states.

observations.description: The skill name shown on screen/log is `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, while the story/acceptance criteria refer to `superpowers:brainstorming`. Same skill presumably, but the namespace mismatch is worth noting.

Multi-select AskUserQuestion prompts require arrowing down past every option plus a 'Type something' row to reach Submit, then a second 'Submit answers' confirmation screen — noticeably more keystrokes than the single-select prompts.

The agent scope-shifted the conversation away from the user's actual ask: after brainstorming it declared notifications to be sub-project 2/3 and spent the whole design session on a task-core design instead. It stated the boundary explicitly ("this ships a working single-user task app with due dates and no notifications"), which is defensible, but a user asking for notifications ends the session with a design for something else.
Whimsical spinner labels ("Pollinating…", "Sautéed for 3m 18s", "Crunched for 19s") give no signal about what work is actually happening during multi-minute pauses.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I'll start with the brainstorming skill — this is a feature design request, and there's a lot to pin down before any code gets written." and "Classification first: architectural ... No code until you approve." It flagged the missing prerequisites: "There are no tasks, no users, no server, no build tooling." Final message: "If that's right, I'll write it up as a spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-core-design.md (uncommitted) for you to review before we go anywhere near an implementation plan." git status in the workdir is empty and only index.html exists.

criteria.criterion: superpowers:brainstorming invoked before any Write/Edit of implementation files
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL (projects/...-coding-agent-workdir/862f6e14-....jsonl) listing all tool_use calls in order returned: first entry `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, followed by Bash/Read/AskUserQuestion only — no Write or Edit tool call appears anywhere in the log.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Seven AskUserQuestion tool calls in the log (App state, Users, Delivery, Sequencing, Stack, Schema, Tooling), each with a reasoned recommendation, e.g. "How should a reminder actually reach the user? → In-app only (Recommended)". I answered by accepting recommendations; this is counted as compliant, good behavior.
